description.text:
This protocol provides sub-surface relationships between
wl_surface objects using token-based identifiers exchanged
out-of-band, instead of the direct wl_surface references
required by wl_subcompositor.  In wl_subcompositor the
parent and sibling surfaces must be local wl_surface objects
from the same client; this protocol removes that
restriction, allowing parent-child relationships both across
different client connections and within the same client:

1. A client exports a wl_surface and receives a surface_token.

2. Another client (or the same client) exports their own
wl_surface and then calls create_remote_subsurface with
the parent's surface_token, attaching their surface as a
child.

All sub-surface semantics follow the wl_subcompositor
specification unless explicitly noted in this document.
Cross-process sub-surfaces are always in desynchronized mode;
synchronized mode is not supported.

This protocol is not interoperable with wl_subsurface: a
wl_subsurface cannot reference a surface that carries a
treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 role, and the two kinds of
sub-surface cannot be ordered relative to each other.  When
a parent surface has both, wl_subsurface is always kept
closest to the parent surface content on each side: a
wl_subsurface placed above the parent content sits below the
treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 children that are above the
parent, and one placed below sits above the
treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 children that are below the
parent.  The relative z-order between the two kinds cannot
be controlled precisely, since place_above and place_below
order treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 children among
themselves and relative to the parent surface content, but
cannot position them relative to wl_subsurface children,
and the wl_subcompositor requests cannot position a
wl_subsurface relative to treeland_remote_subsurface_v1
children.

Clients that need fine-grained z-order control across all
sub-surfaces of a parent should replace wl_subsurface with
treeland_remote_subsurface_v1, which is designed for
cross-process relationships but may equally be used within a
single client, avoiding two separate sub-surface trees that
cannot interact with each other.

The compositor must restrict binding to trusted clients.
A client that obtains a surface_token must only share it
with other trusted clients through a secure mechanism;
the compositor does not disclose tokens to other clients.

The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall",
"shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may",
and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as
described in RFC 2119.

Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

Global factory for exporting wl_surface objects as
token-addressable sub-surface parents or children.

The typical workflow is:

1. The client calls export_surface on a wl_surface to
obtain a treeland_exported_surface_v1 and receive a
surface_token event.

2. The token is shared out-of-band with another client.

3. That client exports its own wl_surface, then calls
create_remote_subsurface with the parent's token to
establish a sub-surface relationship.

Destroying this manager does not affect already-exported
surfaces or existing sub-surface relationships; it only
prevents creation of new exported surfaces.

Destroys this manager object.  Already-exported
treeland_exported_surface_v1 objects and existing
sub-surface relationships are not affected.

Registers a wl_surface as addressable by token,
creating a treeland_exported_surface_v1.  Upon
success the compositor emits the surface_token event
on the new object.

The surface must not have been previously exported
through this manager; doing so is a bad_surface
error.  A surface may carry both an xdg_toplevel (or
any other role) and an export; the export only marks
it as addressable by token.
description.summary: register a surface for token-addressable sub-surface use

entries.name: bad_surface
entries.summary: the wl_surface has already been exported through this manager

description.text:
Represents a wl_surface registered for sub-surface use
via this protocol.  The surface may act as a parent or a
child; a surface can have at most one parent via this
protocol.

Destroying this object revokes the surface_token without
affecting existing parent-child relationships or
treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 objects.
description.summary: an exported surface, addressable by token

description.text:
Revokes the surface_token; subsequent use of the
token in create_remote_subsurface results in an
invalid_token parent_rejected event on the
requesting treeland_exported_surface_v1.

The client must destroy this object before destroying
the associated wl_surface.

Attaches the exported surface to the parent identified
by parent_token, creating a treeland_remote_subsurface_v1.
The surface must not already have a wlroots role; it
will be assigned the exclusive
treeland_remote_subsurface_v1 role.  If the surface
already has an incompatible role, a bad_surface error
is raised and the new treeland_remote_subsurface_v1
object is inert.

If the parent_token is invalid or would introduce a
cycle, the request is ignored and a parent_rejected
event is emitted carrying the reject_reason.

The sub-surface addition is double-buffered on the
parent.
description.summary: attach this surface as a child to a remote parent

args.name: parent_token
args.summary: surface_token of the parent, obtained via export

description.text:
Emitted immediately after export_surface.  The token
is a unique string of at most 128 characters,
generated by a cryptographically secure random number
generator, intended to be shared out-of-band so that
other clients can reference this surface as a parent
or sibling.

Emitted when create_remote_subsurface cannot
establish the requested parent-child relationship.
description.summary: create_remote_subsurface could not attach to the parent

description.text:
These errors can be raised in response to
treeland_exported_surface_v1 requests.

entries.name: bad_surface
entries.summary: the child surface already has an incompatible role

description.text:
Indicates why a create_remote_subsurface request
could not establish the requested parent-child
relationship.

entries.name: invalid_token
entries.summary: parent_token does not identify a live exported surface

entries.name: cyclic
entries.summary: parent_token would introduce a cycle in the sub-surface tree

description.text:
An additional interface to a wl_surface that has been
made a sub-surface via this protocol.  A sub-surface has
one parent and is not automatically clipped to its
parent's area.

Mapping and commit semantics follow wl_subcompositor
except that desynchronized mode is always used.  A
sub-surface never has the keyboard focus of any seat.

The parent is identified at creation time and cannot be
changed.  place_above and place_below accept a token
(string) instead of a wl_surface proxy; see the request
documentation for valid values.

The wl_surface.offset request is ignored; clients must
use set_position instead.
description.summary: remote sub-surface interface to a wl_surface

description.text:
Removes the sub-surface association, unmaps the
wl_surface immediately, and destroys this object.

Schedules a position change relative to the parent
surface coordinate system.  Coordinates are not
restricted to the parent area; negative values are
allowed.  Double-buffered on the parent; replaces any
previous pending position.  Initial position is 0, 0.

args.name: x
args.summary: x coordinate in the parent surface local coordinate system

args.name: y
args.summary: y coordinate in the parent surface local coordinate system

description.text:
Places this sub-surface just above the reference
identified by sibling_token, changing the z-order.
Z-order is double-buffered on the parent surface.
A new sub-surface is initially added at the top.

Valid sibling_token values:

- The surface_token of the parent exported surface.

- The surface_token of any sibling cross-process
sub-surface under the same parent, shared via
out-of-band communication.

- An empty string (""), a sentinel meaning
"place at the very top of the sibling stack".

If the sibling_token does not identify a valid
target, the request is ignored and an
invalid_sibling event is emitted.

args.name: sibling_token
args.summary: a surface_token or empty string for top

description.text:
Places this sub-surface just below the reference
identified by sibling_token.  The same sibling_token
values are accepted as in place_above, except that an
empty string is a sentinel meaning "place at the very
bottom of the sibling stack".

If the sibling_token does not identify a valid
target, the request is ignored and an
invalid_sibling event is emitted.

args.name: sibling_token
args.summary: a surface_token or empty string for bottom

description.text:
Emitted when a sibling_token does not identify a valid
target.  The corresponding restack request was ignored.
description.summary: a place_above or place_below request could not be fulfilled
